notes: Monnify (Moniepoint) payments API. The upstream is the vendor's own OpenAPI 3.0.3, committed in the Monnify GitHub org's mcp-server repo and used there to generate the official MCP server's types; openapi.json is that file rendered to JSON with info.x-openfn-adaptor added and five labelled response keys re-keyed to their status code ("200 - OK" -> 200; "401 - Invalid Token" and "401 - No header" merged as one 401; "200 (With OTP)" and "200 (Without OTP)" merged as one 200), since a Responses Object key must be a status code. The two bvn-*-match operations also document a "99" response, which is a Monnify responseCode rather than an HTTP status; it is left as is because the upstream does not say which status it rides on. It covers 77 operations: auth, transactions/checkout and card charge, transfers (single and bulk disbursements, OTP, summaries, wallet balance), reserved accounts, invoices, recurring card tokens, direct debit mandates, sub-accounts, limit profiles, refunds, settlements, BVN/NIN/account verification, bills payment, banks, wallets and paycodes. The docs portal's own copy (developers.monnify.com/collection/monnify-collection.yml, reportedly OpenAPI 3.1.0 v2.0.0) is behind a Cloudflare block from this environment and could not be compared; it may be newer. Known gaps against the adaptor and vendor SDKs (not added, since upstream is verbatim): POST /api/v1/transaction-notification/resend-failed-notifications (used in the adaptor's post() example), GET /api/v1/direct-debit/mandates and POST /api/v1/merchant/ussd/initialize. Operations carry no operationId and every response is a named whole-envelope schema (requestSuccessful/responseMessage/responseCode/responseBody), so data-schemas lists the *SuccessResponse wrappers as resources; that is the vendor's modelling.
